::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Feb 26th [1864]  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne, Winchester.[^2]  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection, CO171: Box 29[^1]
:::

My dear [Miss Palmer](people/person_1131.qmd)[^3]
I am ashamed of not having thanked you sooner for the statement [C M S](organizations/other_19.qmd) which is a great help to me, being very clear though of course very sad. I think Mr Gorst’s [book](other_books/otherbook_359.qmd) must be soon coming, and then I shall dash into my subject - I was going to say like Captain Dodd at the pirate, for I have just been reading that wonderful chapter of [Hard Cash](other_books/otherbook_360.qmd). Have you heard of [Miss Bennett](people/person_138.qmd) lately. I am afraid her eyes are very much affected. She spent a day with us and was obliged to shade them constantly with a screen and I am afraid they have been worse since that

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: Elderfield added by hand to the printed address.
[^3]: Louisa Catherine Palmer (d. 1868) and [Mary Anne Palmer](people/person_1132.qmd) (d. 1884) were sisters -in-law of the Rev. Charles Abraham, first bishop of Wellington, New Zealand.  They may have supplied CMY with tales of missionary heroism for use in *A Book of Golden Deeds*.
